verses.author: model_A
verses.text: The phone rings twice in an empty house and then stops.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Dust settles back
onto the table
where no one waits

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The porch light burns
for no one's homecoming --
moths keep the watch

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone left keys
on the hook by the door --
still swinging slightly

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A cup of tea cools
its steam thinning to nothing --
the chair still pulled out

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Rain starts outside --
no one runs to bring in
the shirts on the line

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The clothesline sags
with all that quiet water --
evening settles in

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
A moth taps the glass,
mistaking porch light for moon --
no one lets it in

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The kettle's whistle
fades before anyone comes --
steam finds the window

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone left the door
cracked all winter, waiting --
now the cold has names

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
I count the names
one by one on the frost --
none of them answer

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the frost melts by noon
whatever I meant to keep
runs clear down the drain

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
a stranger's boots
by the drain, still dripping --
someone else stayed dry

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I pick up the boots,
try them on for size --
they fit someone I was

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
now I walk in his stride
down streets that don't ask
whose feet these were

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the boots know a shortcut
past the house I grew up in --
I let them lead
